stem: On the same morning a Massachusetts hospital pharmacist begins collaboratively managing an inpatient after a discussion about that patient with the attending supervising physician, and a community pharmacist begins collaboratively managing a walk-in after an identical discussion with her supervising physician. Neither holds a signed individual referral. Which analysis is correct?

choices.text: Both are properly referred, since a consultation is a referral in any setting.
The hospital pharmacist is properly referred; the community pharmacist is not.
The community pharmacist is properly referred; the hospital pharmacist is not.
Neither is properly referred, because a written referral is always required.
Neither is properly referred, because a referral must be signed to be effective.

explanation.core_reasoning: 243 CMR 2.12(1) defines Referral as the individual patient referral by a supervising physician to an authorized pharmacist in a COMMUNITY PHARMACY setting, and IN ALL OTHER PRACTICE SETTINGS as the CONSULTATION of a supervising physician and an authorized pharmacist about a patient for that purpose. The same facts therefore satisfy the definition in the hospital and fail it in the community pharmacy.

choice_analysis.A: The definition changes with the setting, so a consultation does not serve everywhere.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: consultation suffices outside the community pharmacy setting.
choice_analysis.D: A written individual referral is required in the community pharmacy setting only.
choice_analysis.E: Signature is not the distinguishing feature; the setting is.

related_facts: The community-pharmacy written referral must state that written consent was executed
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates carry the community-pharmacy formalities into every setting because those formalities are the ones the regulations describe in detail.

reasoning_steps: Identify the practice setting in each case
Apply the community-pharmacy limb of the definition to the walk-in
Apply the all-other-settings limb to the inpatient
